Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 43-year-old postpartum woman with acute onset shortness of breath and mild tachycardia; advised immediate ED evaluation for possible pulmonary embolism.

History:
- Presenting complaint: New shortness of breath beginning ~1 hour ago while seated; no prior similar episodes.
- Associated symptoms: Dry cough since yesterday; subjective “heart racing”; no chest pain, but chest and C-section scar sore on deep inspiration.
- Pertinent negatives: No sputum, no fever, no calf pain reported.
- Obstetric history: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; uncomplicated postoperative course.
- Past medical history: None reported other than recent C-section.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen – reaction unspecified.
- Medications: Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented); last taken ~1 week ago. Advised to withhold.
- Social / preventive: Caring for 4-week-old infant at home; partner at work. No smoking/alcohol history discussed.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not formally measured; patient pulse counted at 30 beats during clinician-timed interval (clinician interpreted as mildly tachycardic).
- No further physical exam documented.

Impression:
- Suspected pulmonary embolism or other postoperative thromboembolic event causing acute dyspnea and tachycardia in postpartum period.

Plan:
- Patient to proceed to nearest Emergency Department urgently; take infant supplies.
- Ambulance offered; patient elected self-transport.
- Hold further Codeine until evaluated.
- ED expected to perform assessment/imaging and initiate anticoagulation if clot confirmed.
- No additional prescriptions or investigations initiated in teleconsult.

Quality checks:

● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Full vital signs (BP, HR, RR, SpO₂, temperature).
  - Detailed allergy reaction description.
  - Comprehensive medication list and doses.
  - Review of systems beyond respiratory/cardiovascular.
  - Past medical, surgical, family, and social histories not fully explored.

● Internal conflicts: None noted.

● Transcript quality: Clear; occasional minor pauses but clinically adequate.
